Fixed /cap-summary showing four teams on the wrong side of an apron and seventeen with the wrong room magnitude — the apron-room columns were subtracting full team salary instead of excluding pure FA cap holds (§ 1.3), the same basis the MLE-eligibility calc on the same page already used

Fixed the /poopoo cap-sheet report, which had been reading rosters from a repo path that stopped existing when the data moved out — it silently treated every team as empty and reported all ~430 rostered players as missing
Removed 86 stale copies of the build's output from the data-directory root — leftovers from the last R run that nothing served or read, and that one tool was still reading wrong champion data from

Repointed the NBNTV Classics blurb writer at the live build output — it was reading a pre-cutover league-history copy that named every playoff team as champion, and a champion lookup in the retired Shiny project

Decided against reorganising the raw box score files into their own folder — the protections it was meant to buy are already in place, and the change would have touched the one set of files that can't be rebuilt

Fixed: the league history page listed nearly every playoff team as that season's champion. The old build counted playoff wins once per player instead of once per game, so any team with about two wins passed for a title winner
Fixed: three players named Will were recorded as "will" throughout the stats pages
The old R build is kept as a one-command fallback for a full season, in case anything the new one hasn't seen yet — a playoff run, an awards vote — comes out differently

The raw box score files — the one thing here that can't be regenerated — are now append-only: the site refuses any save that would shorten one, rewrite games already recorded, or quietly drop a column an older season keeps
A weekly check now verifies that no completed season's box scores have changed and that no file has lost rows, alerting on Discord and failing loudly if either ever happens
Closed the standing 'nothing backs up the league data' item — the off-box snapshot has been running since yesterday; what's left is a second copy at another provider and a practice restore
Filed a bug: the site has three different answers for which season it is between July and September, which will bite the first time a season starts before October
Every committed game now leaves a record of who submitted it, who entered it and when — the audit trail the box score screenshots used to be, at a fraction of the space
The league data now gets a weekly copy to a second provider, with every member token stripped out of it first but names, roles and tenures kept
Practised restoring the whole site from that backup: it rebuilt all 86 generated files exactly, which is the first real proof the backup is complete
Retired the long-dead stats.nbn.today file mirror, and stopped the backup from carrying live sign-in sessions
The commit check that guards against a page reading a column the build no longer writes now travels with the repo, so a fresh checkout gets it too
Added a deploy script to both live checkouts — it refuses to deploy over uncommitted changes and prints the exact command to roll back
There is now a separate dev copy of the site to work in, so editing a file no longer puts it live the instant it is saved
Pinned the API's dependency list, which did not exist — a fresh checkout can now rebuild the exact same environment and run all 39 test suites green
The deploy script now refuses to run from the dev copy, where it would have pulled into one tree and restarted another
dev.nbn.today is live over HTTPS behind a password, and signing in on the main site now signs you in there too — so committee and team pages can finally be tested before they go live
Wrote a one-page runbook: what lives where, what runs automatically, how to restore from backup, and what to do first when something breaks

Built the test harness for retiring the R stats build: it runs both engines and compares every generated file byte for byte, so a ported piece can only be adopted once it produces exactly what R produced
Confirmed the stats build is deterministic — two runs produce byte-identical output across all 86 files, and a harness run reproduces the live site's data exactly
Corrected the project guide, which still described data files as living in this repo — they moved out yesterday, and the guide is what every future session reads first
Started replacing the R stats build with Python: the head-to-head record tables are now generated by the new code and match the old output exactly, byte for byte
Matched R's exact number and text formatting first, so every future piece of the port is checked against the old build rather than eyeballed — 159,363 numbers verified identical
Career totals and single-game high leaderboards are now generated by the new Python build too — 14 of the 86 generated files, every one matching the old output exactly
The whole stats build now has a Python implementation — all 86 generated files, checked against the old build file by file
Found and fixed a broken league history file: it listed eleven champions for the 2020-21 season because it counted a team's playoff wins once per player instead of once per game
Fixed three players (Will Barton, Will Richard, Will Riley) whose first name was being lower-cased to "will" everywhere on the site
Fixed the daily Perry and Poeltl games, the Discord stats commands and the waiver standings lookup, all of which broke when data moved out of the site repo yesterday
Wrote down where the stats rebuild stands, so the switch-over can be picked up cleanly: the new build is finished and checked, the old one is still the one running
Data files no longer live in the site repo: the stats build writes to the data directory and nginx serves from there, so this repo is now purely code and deploys are a plain git pull
No change to any URL, page or CSV — every file the site fetches is served from the same address as before
Deleted 650 lines of dead code from the stats build, including every remaining line that could pull rosters from a Google Sheet — the build can no longer make a network call at all
Measured the build for the first time: 22 seconds, not the 10 minutes assumed, and it provably touches only generated files (rosters, bios and the transaction ledger are untouched)

Planned the retirement of the R stats build (docs/stats-pipeline-port-spec.md): port the aggregation to Python in the API, keep the full-recompute model, and require byte-identical output as the acceptance test
Team logos are now real files in this repo instead of symlinks into the retired stats app, so the site no longer depends on a project it has outgrown (pixels unchanged)
Added a 10-minute snapshot job that commits the league data and pushes it off-box, with a guard that refuses to mirror a mass deletion into the backup

Specced the dev/live split and data layout (docs/dev-deploy-setup-spec.md): work moves to -dev checkouts with git pull as the deploy step, the R build stops writing into the git working tree, and the box score data gets a real backup story

Backed up the league data off-box for the first time — all six seasons of box scores, the transaction ledger, rosters and member records now push to a private repo, verified byte-identical by clone-back diff and checksum
Locked down the credential files (members.json, sessions.json, tokens.json) to owner-only, and fixed the API's atomic write so it stops resetting file permissions on every save
Added a Discord trade-vote scraper and tally page (/tradevotes, unlisted) scoring reactors FOR/AGAINST each team named in a trade by their reaction emoji

Documented the § 6.2 extension pipeline plan (docs/poext-extension-pipeline.md), reserved the Agent and POEXT/POEXT_HEAD committee roles on /roles and /members, and recorded ledger-derived eligibility findings in BACKLOG.md

"Clean Up the Poo Poo" now awards a new Archivist achievement tier for approved submissions, and gained a second gap type: 162 flagged Discord FA-signing candidates, answered by identifying the player and approved into the real transaction ledger

Re-keyed 27 of 29 first-last player slugs to the canonical last-first form across bios, OVR history, transactions, roster/dead-cap CSVs, and player attributes; 2 players with a live FFA window held back for a follow-up pass

Added "Clean Up the Poo Poo" (/cleanup) — members submit fixes for missing player bio facts (height, wingspan, weight, college, country, DOB, photo, draft info), admin reviews and approves, approval pays tiered NB¥

Fixed the computed starting five (depth chart) locking a dual-eligible player into the earlier of his two positions regardless of what that stranded at the later one — e.g. a C/PF big always claiming PF over a higher center rating; it now maximizes the lineup's total OVR instead of optimizing position-by-position in PG→C order

Non-guaranteed contract years can now carry a multi-step guarantee schedule (specific dates/amounts that vest over time) instead of a single partial-guarantee figure — added a step editor to the team-facing FA offer form on /free-agency and surfaced the schedule on hover in the PDC review page's per-offer year table

Renounce (§ 3.10) now also covers a team's unsigned draft rights to a player it drafted but never signed (§ 7.1), not just a UFA/RFA cap hold — updated the roster-page renounce dialog, eligibility check, and rulebook language to match
Surfaced waiver-wire transactions (claimed/unclaimed clearances and PDC-flagged ties) in the /transactions log with dedicated badges, filters, and detail text
Made RFA vs UFA status visually distinct in the PDC dashboard — gold badges in the player list and player detail header, where both used to render as identical plain text/chips

Added a member inbox: a new /inbox page plus a mailbox button in the nav (next to the theme picker) with an unread badge, backed by GET/POST /api/inbox on the API; members now get a notification for role/tenure changes, suggestion status changes and comments, FA offer remand/void/restore and finalize, waiver claim results, and being sent an FA player back from committee review

The office's contract form gained a § 3.12 minimum-contract generator (start season, guaranteed years, trailing option/hold) that pulls dollar figures straight off that season's minimum salary scale instead of typing them in by hand, including the § 3.12 one-year veteran-minimum hardship cap

Fixed a gap where `sign` accepted a contract with zero salary years, silently wiping any existing cap hold and leaving the player on the roster with no salary; both the live rubric and the submit path now refuse it
Fixed the minimum-salary check disagreeing with the cap-hit check on a correctly hardship-capped one-year veteran minimum — both now agree on the same figure

Reversed the minimum-scale model to price every year of a multi-year minimum contract flat off the declared experience tier (matching the league's own rosters sheet) instead of climbing a tier per contract year

The transactions log's type filter now has pills for Two-Way Conversions, Voids, and Hard Cap Sets — those three types were fully wired into the feed and the entry form but had no way to isolate them via the filter row

Offer sheet decisions (matched/not matched) now render with a proper "Offer Sheet Decision" badge, team columns, and a details cell showing the contract and who signed — previously the badge fell back to the raw type string and the team/details columns were blank because the renderer didn't know that type stores its teams under `teams` rather than `team`

The office's Signing Method field now hides itself when a sign's contract type is two-way, since a two-way carries no funding method to declare — it was previously left visible and looked required for a field the validator ignores

Added the waiver wire design spec (docs/waiver-wire-spec.md) — a 48-hour claim window on every release, with priority by worst qualifying record and a head-to-head tiebreak. Design only; nothing implemented yet on this side

Free agency has a third committee role: agents. A free agent whose offer window closes now goes to the agents before any sub-committee sees him — they claim him off a shared queue, negotiate the offers down, and either advance the survivors to a ballot or finalize an uncontested one

Claiming a player is exclusive and opens every offer on him in full. An agent cannot claim a player their own team is bidding on, and claiming one permanently bars that team from bidding on him — the bar survives releasing the claim and survives the player being reopened

Sending an offer back for revision is now the agent's, along with voiding one; assigned sub-committee members no longer do either. The FAC head keeps both everywhere, and can send an advanced player back to his agent with a reason

Nothing is balloted until an agent advances the slate. Ballots already cast survive a send-back and are flagged for their members rather than discarded, the same way a revision or a void already flagged them

The PDC dashboard has an agent view: the queue of players waiting to be picked up, with blocked ones shown greyed and the reason on them, and offer counts hidden on the players your own team is bidding on

The office's contract helper now generates a trailing UFA/RFA hold row for the season after the deal ends (§ 3.10), matching what the team-facing FA offer form already did — it used to only produce the guaranteed/option years, leaving every helper-built contract with no recorded status after it expired

Fixed the signing form showing the wrong MLE tier (e.g. NTMLE instead of Taxpayer MLE) for teams whose exception bucket hadn't been used yet this season — it now agrees with what the team page already showed

Signing a free agent or building an RFA offer sheet now defaults to a preset raise off Year 1 (-8%/-5%/flat/+5%/+8%) instead of free-typed year-by-year salaries, on both the office's transaction form and the team-facing FA offer form. Custom amounts are still available, just behind an explicit "enter custom amounts" checkbox. Minimum-salary deals and rookie-scale pick signings are unaffected — they keep pricing off their own scales

The /tradeblock save panel has an off-by-default "Also post to Discord" checkbox that announces what a team added and removed in that save — manual edits only; a player coming off the block automatically (e.g. traded away) stays silent

Adding a transaction now has a toggle for whether it also gets mirrored into #roster-log, off by default — most transactions are already typed into that channel by hand while being worked, so the automatic mirror only needs to fire for the ones that aren't

The FAC head can give a player's free-agency window more time without throwing away the bidding that has already happened. Every offer already submitted stands, the sub-committee's ballots stay exactly as cast, and only the deadline moves

This works on a window that has already closed, which is the case it was built for — reopening a lapsed window used to mean starting a fresh round, which quietly left the votes already cast behind. Extending a closed window counts the hours from now, so "six more hours" means six more hours either way

Both ways of putting a player back in front of teams now sit together on the head's own controls on that player's page, with the difference spelled out: extending keeps the round as it stands, while opening the player starts a genuine second window with a clean ballot. Previously the reopen was only reachable from the "+ Player" picker, which skips anyone already on the board — that is, exactly the players a head would want to reopen — and the Open button gave no hint that it would discard the ballots

Extending requires a reason, and that reason is shown to every team along with the new deadline, in the public free-agency channel as well as the committee one. A deadline that moves without explanation is worse than one that doesn't move
The window's stated length follows it, so a window extended from 24 hours to 30 stops describing itself as a 24-hour window everywhere it is named

The rookie scale is on the site. /rookie-scale has always existed and has never had anything in it, so every first-round pick signing was typed in by hand off the spreadsheet; it now holds the real per-pick figures for the 2025 and 2026 drafts, and it is a normal page in the nav rather than something only the League Office could reach

Each pick shows five figures, not four: the four contract years (Years 3 and 4 as team options) plus the RFA cap hold the deal rolls into under § 3.10, which is 250% or 300% of the Year 4 salary depending on where that salary sits against the season's average. The hold is part of what the scale prescribes, so it is shown with it, and each row names the seasons it applies to

Signing a first-round pick on /transactions now fills the contract in for you — all five years, with the option and hold tags already set, from that player's own draft slot. The rows stay editable, so an off-scale deal is still possible if the league has ruled that way; it will just be flagged as off-scale

Draft pick signings are checked before they are submitted. They previously ran no checks at all: a pick signing could put a team over its hard cap or past the roster limit and the system would accept it without comment, despite § 1.3 saying it blocks exactly that. It now checks the hard cap, the roster ceiling, that the player really does hold unsigned draft rights, and that the terms match the § 7.1 scale year by year — live, as you type, the same way a free-agent signing has been
Second-round picks say so rather than sitting silent — they are not on the scale, so the form explains the § 7.1 structure to enter instead of pretending it has nothing to offer

The "prior salary vs. EAPS" question is only asked when it changes a number. It was being shown on every contract, and it only ever matters for a Full Bird cap hold in a season with no average-salary figure on file — which is a small minority of signings. It now appears when the hold actually needs it, stays put once answered, and disappears if the hold does

The 2024 rookie scale is deliberately not loaded: its cap-hold multiplier runs the opposite way to 2025 and 2026, giving the biggest holds to the most expensive contracts, and the league sheet and the site disagree about two players. Nothing about the 2024 contracts themselves is in question — only the 28-29 holds — and it is on the backlog pending a fix to the sheet

The four channels a roster-log entry can come from — #fa-news, #transactions, #waivers and the site’s own #roster-log-nbn-today — are now mirrored into #roster-log automatically, within a minute of the message being posted. That copying was being done by hand, from four places, which is the kind of job that gets skipped on a busy day

The mirror relays, it never interprets: the message that lands in #roster-log is the source message’s own text, unedited. It doesn’t summarise, doesn’t re-parse a contract, and doesn’t try to judge whether a message counts as a transaction — a human reads the line and enters it, and a wrong paraphrase there is worse than a line that turned out not to need entering

Only humans are mirrored from #fa-news, since the site’s own FFA clock posts there are not sheet changes; everything the humans post is, including the team options and guarantees a keyword filter would have dropped. The site’s own transaction posts are mirrored in full, flattened from a card to text and keeping their year-by-year salary breakdown
Each entry arrives as a plain bordered card carrying nothing but the text, so consecutive entries have an edge — a multi-line trade followed by three one-line renounces used to read as one blob
Role pings survive the trip as text but no longer notify anyone a second time, and a message forwarded into a source channel is mirrored as what it forwarded rather than as an empty message

Nothing is mirrored retroactively: the mirror starts from the moment it is switched on and skips anything older than a day, so it can never dump a channel’s history into #roster-log. Carrying an older message across is deliberate and admin-only

PDC free agency: the FAC head sets how long an FFA window runs, in hours (1–168, default 24), next to the mode switch. It applies to clocks started from then on — a clock already running keeps the deadline it was stamped with, so changing the setting can never move a deadline teams are already bidding against or close an open window early

Every place that named the FFA window's length now reads it off the clock being described rather than a fixed 24 — the refusal a team sees on a closed player, both Discord clock posts, and the dashboard — so changing the setting mid-round doesn't rewrite the history of windows that already ran

§ 3.12 now states that a minimum contract tracks the scale: its salary in any season is the applicable minimum for that season, not the figure written when it was signed. The Minimum Salary Scale is re-set each league year, so a revision is worth real money to every minimum deal running through that season. The rulebook also says plainly that nothing re-prices those contracts automatically yet — the amounts are refreshed by hand, and a deal running past a revised season reads at its old figures until someone does it

Cap Settings can now add seasons beyond the next one. It showed the current league year plus one, which is shorter than the contracts being written against it — § 3.12 prices each year of a minimum deal on its own season's scale, so the out-years of a multi-year deal need real seasons to sit on

A contract can now state the player's years of NBA experience as of its first season, and § 3.12 prices every year off that, stepping up one scale row per contract year. Without it a multi-year minimum for a veteran sat flat at the rookie minimum for all of its years: the tier was inferred from the stored draft year, which is the NBN draft and is blank for every player who entered the league before it — 121 of the 212 current free agents, including a 12-year veteran who priced $2.5M/yr light. The signing forms ask for it on minimum deals, prefilled from the draft year where there is one, and the committee sees the declared figure on the offer card

A signing priced in minimum territory for a player whose experience can't be established now warns instead of reporting a clean pass. The tier check returned "can't tell" and the validator then said "every contract year meets the § 3.12 minimum salary" — which is how the flat veteran minimum above went through without comment

A multi-year minimum contract is no longer rejected for breaking the 5% raise rule. § 3.12 says each year of a minimum deal pays that season's Minimum Salary Scale figure for the player's experience, and at the bottom of the scale one tier to the next is a 61% jump — the § 3.13 raise ladder was being applied to it anyway, so the contract the rulebook prescribes couldn't be offered. Minimum-scale years are now exempt from the ladder; a deal that starts at the minimum and then leaps above the scale is still an error

The offer form's Minimum fill now climbs the scale year by year instead of repeating Year 1 flat, and re-derives when the contract length changes — a 1-year minimum's cap hit (the 2-year veteran minimum) isn't the right Year 1 for a 3-year deal
Anyone on a team's front office can now submit a free-agent offer, not just the owner — whoever can draft an offer can send it to the committee
Removed the "Only the team owner can submit this offer" block on the offer form; submit is still disabled while a rule check fails or the player isn't accepting offers

§ 2.2's three-slot two-way limit is now enforced. Two-way signings previously passed validation having run zero checks — the standard roster check is skipped for them (they sit outside the 15) and every other check no-ops on a $0 salary — so a fourth two-way went through clean on both the offer form and the office's submit path

Fixed a roster-count off-by-one on signings: a team's own free agent stays on the roster CSV, so re-signing him counted him twice and reported a roster one larger than the signing would actually produce. Affected the roster-size warning on 13 live free-agent offers

A funding method is now required on every standard-contract signing (§ 3.1–3.6). A blank method wasn't checked against anything — the funding validator returns early for any method it doesn't recognise, and "none" was one of them — so a signing could pass with no demonstrated way to pay for it. Two-way contracts are exempt: $0, outside Team Salary (§ 2.2)

PDC free agency: the "nobody is assigned" prompt now fires on a closed FFA window, which is when sub-committees are actually assigned. It was keyed on a player status that FFA never sets, so it had never appeared for an FFA player

PDC free agency: the player queue now leads with the players whose 24-hour window has closed and are waiting on a sub-committee, longest-waiting first — previously they sorted below every player still collecting offers, which is backwards for the phase the list exists to run. Finalized players sort last instead of staying at the top forever

Season Stats has a "Rookies only" filter — rookie seasons of anyone drafted 2020 or later, combinable with the season and team filters. Players with no NBN draft year on file are excluded, since the data can't separate an undrafted rookie from a veteran who joined mid-history

Fixed the Add Player form deriving the wrong slug: it asked for "Last, First" and then generated a first-last key (keaton-wallace instead of wallace-keaton), which split the player's stats from their bio. Slugs now match the site-wide last-first convention

Fixed the trade validator scoring teams that don't exist: an unknown abbreviation was reported as passing its hard-cap check with a roster count of -1, so a trade whose salaries happened to match could have come back LEGAL for a team that isn't in the league
Added the first tests that call the /api/validate/* endpoints over HTTP rather than the validator functions underneath them — the layer where both of this week's simulator bugs actually lived

Transactions: added the § 3.10 EAPS question the API needs to price a Full Bird cap hold. Without it, re-signing any 3+ year tenured player into a trailing UFA/RFA hold was rejected at submit with an error naming a field this page didn't have

Transactions: signings now get a live rubric — the same POST /api/validate/sign the simulator and the FA offer form use, with the trailing hold's dollar figure — instead of no check at all until submit
Transactions: an option decline no longer demands a hand-typed cap hold amount; left blank the API computes the § 3.10 figure, and the box is an override

Transactions: contract summaries in the log now read "2+1 PO, $150M" like the rest of the site, and no longer count a trailing UFA/RFA hold as a contract year (which inflated both the year count and the total)

Fixed POST /api/validate/offer_sheet returning a 500 on every call — it still read an `outcome` field that was removed when offer sheets were split into two transactions. The simulator's offer-sheet mode was broken by the same bug

New shared contract.js: one cap-hold vocabulary and one shorthand grammar for team pages, the PDC dashboard and the transactions log, replacing three copies of the same code. The Discord embeds' Python version is now pinned to it by a test

FA offers: the § 3.10 cap hold a contract rolls into is now priced live as you build the deal, instead of reading "amount computed by the office" — the figure moves with the years, salaries, Bird tier and EAPS toggle, and is restated on the submit confirmation
Transaction simulator: the "Rolls into" row now carries the hold's dollar amount
PDC dashboard: the committee's year table now shows the trailing UFA/RFA hold and what it costs — previously the hold season was missing from the reviewed deal entirely
API: new fact_sheet.trailing_hold on POST /api/validate/sign and /api/validate/offer_sheet, priced by the same helper that writes the hold at signing time, so no surface computes it independently
FA offers: choosing the Minimum method now auto-fills the § 3.12 figures for that player rather than leaving the salary boxes at $0
FA offers: salary boxes accept pasted figures with $ and commas instead of silently zeroing

Signings no longer hard-block a team sitting at 15 standard players: § 2.1's offseason shape (≤15 passes, 16-20 warns, >20 blocks) now applies to FA signings, offer sheets and two-way conversions, matching what a trade adding the same player already allowed
Fixed the Bi-Annual Exception showing as available to a team that had already used it that season
Rulebook: § 7.2 badge updated to 🔒 system-enforced + 👁 manual review, reflecting the live Stepien Rule check; added a note distinguishing it from the still-unenforced 7-year advance limit
Homepage: added an admin-only Backlog nav card linking to the new /backlog page
Backlog: new /backlog page renders BACKLOG.md for admins

PDC dashboard: reworked the head-only controls into a single boxed "FAC Head controls" zone instead of scattering badges per control; renamed queue/board labels to "My free agents"/"All players"; added role-chip tooltips explaining what each committee role grants
Members: added role badge styles for fac/fac_head/poext/poext_head

Frivolities earnings tab: only count guaranteed salary (mirrors _apply_release's dead-cap logic) instead of full contract face value, so UFA/RFA holds, team options, and non-guaranteed years no longer inflate career earnings
Rulebook: a trade funded purely by cap-room absorption (§ 4.2) no longer triggers the § 4.3/§ 4.4 apron contagion hard cap, matching how the real NBA treats cap-space acquisitions
Cleared DEN's incorrectly-triggered First Apron hard cap from the Keldon Johnson trade
The committee head's "+ Player" picker now lists only the players who are actually free agents this league year, instead of everyone with a cap hold on file — and says how many it left out and why
Renounced and never-signed players count as free agents right now, whichever season they were filed under

Fixed: the free-agency offer menu treated every player with a cap hold on file as available, including the 361 still under contract whose hold lands in a future season. Only players who have actually reached free agency this league year can be offered a contract; the rest say which season they become free agents
The committee head is likewise blocked from opening a player who hasn't reached free agency yet

Team front offices can now draft and submit free-agency offers from /free-agency: a ⋯ menu on each free agent opens a contract editor with year-by-year salary, options, the trailing cap hold, funding method and Bird tier, plus a pitch and the promises (minutes, role, playoffs) the committee reads alongside the money
The offer is checked against the rulebook live as you type, by the same validator the office runs — an offer that fails a rule can't be submitted, and warnings are shown but don't block
Any member of a team's front office can prepare the offer; only the team owner can submit it, and the button says so rather than disappearing
The form shows what the team has already committed across all its live offers against its room, since a pending offer holds no cap room
Submitting takes a second confirm step naming the player, the years and the total: once submitted to the committee an offer cannot be withdrawn (§ 3.14)
When the committee sends an offer back for changes, the row is flagged and the form reopens with every reviewer's note pinned above the editor and the previous figures shown beside each year
Players who aren't taking offers show the reason — free agency closed, not open this round, or the 24-hour window having lapsed — instead of a menu entry that does nothing
Nothing on this page changes for a visitor who isn't signed in to a team

Committee members can now cast their 1,000 balls on the PDC dashboard: a slider and a number per offer, plus the qualifying offer for a restricted free agent and a "no signing" line always, with a running remainder and saving blocked until it totals exactly 1,000
Each line on the ballot carries the deal it stands for, and flags an offer that's been sent back or has gone illegal since it was made
Ballots stay editable until the head locks the player, and a member whose ballot predates a revision is told so rather than having their vote discarded

FAC heads can finalize a player: a confirm step showing the running totals, who voted, who will be recorded as abstaining, and any remand the team never answered — which warns but never blocks. Unlock reverses it

Finalizing records the committee's decision and frees those teams to bid again in a later round. It signs nobody — the signing is still entered by hand on the transactions page, and the dashboard says so
A collapsible "How this works" panel explains the pipeline, sectioned by whether you're a committee member, the head, or both

Committee members can find the dashboard from the site search (Ctrl+K) instead of remembering the address — it's listed only for members who hold the role, and a signed-out visitor's search works exactly as before

Free-agency events now post to Discord: the committee's private channel gets every offer in full (contract year by year, funding method, promises, pitch and the legality verdict), plus remands with their note, mode and round changes, clock starts and expiries, and the final ballot allocation
A resubmitted offer is announced with a diff against the version the committee actually sent back — and says so plainly when a resubmission changed nothing

In free-for-all mode the league channel gets exactly two posts per player: the 24-hour clock starting, and the window closing. Never a team, a figure, or an offer count — who is bidding stays committee information
Deadlines post as Discord timestamps, so every reader sees the 24-hour window in their own timezone
Both channels stay silent until they're configured, and each is independent of the other

New committee dashboard at /pdc for the Free Agency Committee: the queue of players you're assigned to, every offer on a player side by side with its contract, legality, promises, pitch and the offering team's projected starting five, and the ballots already cast
FAC heads can set the free-agency mode, open rounds, open/hold/close a player, and assign a sub-committee — with any member whose own team is bidding flagged before the assignment is confirmed
Any assigned reviewer can send an offer back to the team for revision with a note, and the offer's revision history shows what moved between versions
An offer that was legal when it was submitted but isn't any more is badged as such, since a submitted offer can't be withdrawn
The page is unlinked and role-gated — without a committee role it shows nothing but a 'forbidden' notice
The dashboard now has its own address, pdc.nbn.today, alongside nbn.today/pdc. Signing in on nbn.today signs you in there too, so committee members can go straight to it
Internal: signing in on nbn.today now signs you in across every nbn.today subdomain, so an upcoming committee page won't ask for your token a second time. Nothing changes on any existing page
Internal: the depth-chart logic that picks a team's starting five moved into its own file so pages other than a team page can use it. Team pages render exactly as before

Groundwork for the Free Agency Committee's review pipeline: the API can now hold contract offers, send one back to a team for revision, and record the committee's 1,000-ball votes. Nothing on the site shows any of it yet and no owner can submit an offer — the tools to review offers have to exist before the first one arrives

Free Agency page: the list of who counts as a free agent now comes from the API instead of being worked out in the browser, so the page and the upcoming committee board can never disagree about it. The page looks and reads exactly as before

Members: four new roles can be granted — FAC and FAC head (free agency), PO-EXT and PO-EXT head (player options and extensions). They are the first piece of the Player Development Committee review pipeline and do nothing yet on their own
Groundwork only: the committee dashboard these roles will gate is specified but not built, so nothing on the site changes for anyone today

Suggestions: every suggestion now has a comment thread, so a suggestion can be followed up on as it's worked rather than only filed and closed. Anyone signed in can comment, on any status — including after it's complete

Suggestions: status changes are recorded in the thread ("chair moved this to In Progress"), so a suggestion carries its own history. Comments can be edited or deleted by whoever wrote them, or by BOD; status entries are the record and can't be

Suggestions can now be edited from the page. The server has accepted edits since the board launched, but nothing in the UI ever offered it. Authors can edit while a suggestion is open; once BOD has triaged it the Edit button stays visible but disabled, saying so and pointing at the comment thread

Team pages: every player on your own roster now has a ⋯ menu (Rosters and Contracts views) for roster moves you're entitled to make. Moves you can't make on that player stay visible but disabled, with the rule that blocks them

Team pages now have a Sign in button when you're not signed in. Previously the only way to enter your token here was a button that already required being signed in, so team owners who aren't on the committee could never reach their own tools
Trade block: add or remove a player straight from your roster, with an optional note for other teams — no more editing the whole block on /tradeblock just to list one player

Renounce (§ 3.10): team owners can now renounce their own free-agent cap holds. The confirmation shows the cap room it frees, the roster count you'd be left with against the 14-player minimum and 12-player charge floor, and the Bird Rights you'd forfeit — then asks you to type the player's name
Renouncing is owner-only. A GM or coach with the team's token can edit the trade block but cannot renounce; legality is re-checked on the server and cannot be forced through
Renounces are now checked against § 3.10 rather than accepted unvalidated, and the same checks back a new public /api/validate/renounce

Rescission (§ 3.10) is implemented: every renounce records what it erased, and the committee can restore a renounced free agent with the undo button on the Transactions log — previously this had to be repaired by hand

Discord: every transaction submitted on the site now posts to a league channel as it happens — teams, player, contract terms, trade assets, and who submitted it. Transactions forced past a failed rulebook check say so

Signings post the full year-by-year salary breakdown alongside the summary, with player options, team options and non-guaranteed years labelled on the year they fall in, and the cap hold the deal rolls into. Contract shorthand matches the roster page ("2+1 PO")

Offer sheet messages now name the team the player actually ends up with. The old header joined the two teams with an arrow, which read backwards on an unmatched offer — the player leaves for the offering team, not the incumbent

Offer sheets (§ 3.15) are now two steps: extending the offer, then the incumbent's decision to match. They're two decisions by two different teams, and recording them as one attributed the match to whoever typed it
An extended offer sits on the books as pending — the offering team carries a cap hold equal to its first-year salary until it's resolved, so a team can't float offers it couldn't collectively fund

Open offer sheets appear at the top of the Transactions page and on both teams' pages, with the 48-hour deadline and an overdue flag. Nothing resolves on a timer — an expired offer nags until someone settles it
Matching is now checked against the incumbent's hard cap. A team may go over the Cap to keep its own free agent, but a hard cap still binds — nothing verified that before

Fixed: offer sheets never counted toward Bird Rights, so a player who changed teams on an unmatched offer kept their tenure credited to the team they left. Mark Williams' Toronto tenure was reading as Minnesota's
Notifications only ever fire for a live submission. Backfilled history, replayed entries and bulk imports send nothing

Busy days are handled properly: messages are paced and queued rather than fired all at once, so a draft day's 50+ moves all arrive (over a couple of minutes) instead of being dropped by Discord's rate limit

Rulebook § 3.9: removed a dangling "§ 8(e)(2)" citation from the extend-and-trade raise row — the rulebook has Articles I–VII only, so it pointed at nothing. The 5% figure is unchanged; defining the extend-and-trade mechanism is now tracked in the backlog
Transaction Simulator: contracts can now carry options — each year can be marked a player option, team option, or non-guaranteed, and the deal can be given a trailing UFA or RFA cap hold (§ 3.10)

The trailing hold's dollar figure is computed by the system from the prior salary and Bird tier rather than typed in, with an optional EAPS assumption for Full Bird holds in seasons with no EAPS on file
Signing results now echo back the option years and the hold the contract rolls into, so the shape being judged is visible

Transaction Simulator: the player dropdown now lists only players who can actually receive the transaction — 301 signable free agents instead of all 1,018 bios, with retired and under-contract players excluded, and each entry labelled with its team and hold type
RFA offer sheets now list only genuine restricted free agents (32), since under § 3.15 nobody else can receive one

§ 3.12 minimum salary is now enforced — a contract year below the Minimum Salary Scale is caught instead of passing clean; salaries between the league floor and the player's own experience tier warn, and two-way contracts are exempt
In-season signings prorate, so a below-minimum Year 1 warns rather than blocks; later contract years are always full seasons and are blocked
Signing a retired player, or a player under contract to another team, is now rejected on both the simulator and real submissions

§ 3.8 Bird Rights tenure is now verified instead of taken on faith — the declared tier is checked against continuous service derived from the transaction ledger, on both real submissions and the Transaction Simulator

Bird tenure follows the actual rule: rights carry through trades (§ 6.2), re-signing your own free agent continues the clock, and signing elsewhere or a release resets it; a drafted player's clock starts at their draft

Only over-claiming is blocked. Claiming a lower tier is allowed, and where tenure can't be established the office gets a warning to check by hand rather than a false verdict — 483 of 487 rostered players resolve
Closed a hole where declaring "Bird Rights" as the funding method skipped cap validation entirely and quietly raised the annual raise ceiling from 5% to 8%
Using Bird Rights on a player the ledger shows with another team is now rejected — Bird Rights re-sign a team's own free agent
Rulebook § 3.8 is now badged system-enforced, with a note on exactly what is and isn't checked
Trade Simulator is now the Transaction Simulator at /transaction-sim/ — pick a transaction type from the tab bar; old /trade-sim/ links redirect and keep their query params

Transaction Simulator: added FA signing — choose team, player, contract years and per-year salary, funding method (§ 3.1–§ 3.6) and Bird tier, then see the same checks the league office runs at submission

Transaction Simulator: added RFA offer sheets — validated against whichever team actually ends up signing the player (retaining team on a match, offering team otherwise), including the roster-spot difference between the two

Signing analysis shows the team's cap position before and after: Team Salary with and without cap holds, cap room, unrenounced free-agent holds, apron position, room to the hard cap, remaining exception balance, and roster count
Per-year raise percentages are shown as you type, with Flat / 5% / 8% fill buttons; Year 1 seeds from the player's current salary
The simulator remains read-only — the new /api/validate/sign and /api/validate/offer_sheet endpoints never write, and there is no path from the simulator to an actual transaction submission
Backlog: refreshed against live data — cap-sheet diffs now 31 across 12 teams, and the stuck changelog entries are tracked by date instead of by index
Add BACKLOG.md — internal working list of open data-integrity items, rule-automation gaps, and tooling debt, not linked from nav
Transactions form: RFA offer sheets now capture a Signing Method (and Bird Rights subtype) alongside the contract, matching what `sign`/`convert_twoway` already collect
Transactions log and player pages: an offer sheet's signing method (MLE / NTMLE / TMLE / Room Exception / BAE / Bird Rights subtype) now shows next to the contract and match/no-match outcome
enter-transaction skill: document the § 3.10 trailing FA-hold pattern (eaps_assumption, never hand-write a placeholder dollar figure) so it's captured alongside the auto-fill it describes

Cap Settings: the League Year "Save" and "Reset to Jul 1" controls now confirm before taking effect immediately — they explain that an immediate rollover switches the live league year everywhere on the site and permanently locks in every team's Room Exception eligibility (§ 3.2) off their Team Salary at that exact moment

Team pages: new "Rosters" view — a depth chart with a starting five (highest-rated eligible PG, SG, SF, PF and C, one slot each) followed by the bench in OVR order. It's now the default view, ahead of Contracts / Stats / Ratings
Rosters view: a player only qualifies for a slot if it's one of their eligible positions, and the five are picked to fill as many slots as possible — the only C on the roster won't get stranded at SF

Rosters view: a "Contract" column summarizing each deal in one line — "2+1 PO, $150M" for two guaranteed years plus a player option, "1+1 TO", "1+1 NG+1 TO", or just "UFA hold" for a player carrying nothing but a cap hold

Trade sheet export: each team's block now shows what it *receives* (Players In / Picks In, with who sent them), not just what it sends — in a three-team deal you had to scan every other block's "To" column to work that out

Trade sheet export: new "Thru" column giving the last season each player is under contract for, flagged PO / TO / NG for option and non-guaranteed years — a $40M expiring and a $40M with four years left no longer look identical
Trade sheet export: a Notes section under each team explaining why any verdict isn't a clean pass, instead of leaving the reason on the Validation tab

Trade Simulator: new "Create Google Sheet" button turns the evaluated trade into a public Google Sheet and hands you the link — no Google sign-in or permission prompt. Laid out like the league's NBN Trade Machine sheet: one block per team with assets out, destinations, and that team's cap summary
There's also a ".xlsx" button next to it if you'd rather have the file

The export carries a Validation tab (every check the office runs, with its verdict) and a Rules tab regenerated from the live cap levels and the rulebook's § 4.2 tiers, so a saved copy can't go stale the way the old hand-maintained sheet did
Trade Simulator now shows Max Incoming, Unaggregated outgoing, and whether a deal needs salary aggregation — computed by the same validator that judges the trade
Fixed hyphenated and apostrophe names rendering as "Gilgeous-alexander" in the trade simulator

Trade builder: an exception can now be applied to specific incoming players rather than a team's whole incoming total — check off which players the MLE or Room Exception is absorbing (rulebook § 4.2a)
This makes hybrid trades enterable: some incoming players matched against outgoing salary, another funded out of the exception
Fixed the Room Exception being refused for teams that were assigned it on July 1 and later went over the cap — § 3.2 locks the assignment for the year
Dates across the site now use league time (US Eastern) instead of UTC — entering a transaction in the evening no longer prefills tomorrow's date
Every date field (transactions, box score submission, OVR updates, strikes, news publishing, calendar) now agrees on the same league day no matter where you are
Calendar: fixed the month view opening a day early for anyone east of UTC
League-year rollover and the season cutoff now happen at midnight Eastern rather than 8pm Eastern the evening before

Frivolities: new Career Earnings tab — every player ranked by total salary on record, split into money banked through the current season and money still owed, with years, AAV, peak salary year and a season-by-season salary sparkline
Career Earnings is filterable by name, team and roster status (including off-roster players and dead-cap contracts) and every column sorts
Salary tracking in NBN begins with 25-26, so the tab counts career earnings on record only — noted on the page itself

Team pages: new Franchise Records section on the All-Time Players tab — each franchise's five best single games for points, rebounds, assists, steals, blocks, threes and Game Score, with opponent, season and a badge for playoff performances

Franchise Records covers every team, unlike the league-wide Single-Game Highs leaderboards a franchise without an all-time great never cracks; playoff games count, and 12% of the records league-wide are playoff performances
Build writes data/franchise-records.csv (top 5 per team per stat, all 30 teams in one file) and the smoke test now checks it

Trade Exceptions (§4.1a) are now created automatically: completing a trade banks a TPE for every over-the-cap team that sent out more salary than it took back, dated to the trade and expiring 365 days later — previously they could only be entered by hand from the league spreadsheet

Rulebook §4.1a: teams under the Salary Cap bank no Trade Exception, matching the real CBA — their cap room already absorbs the difference, so granting one on top would let the same space be spent twice
Hard cap §1.4 Row D is now automated: signing a player whose contract was terminated earlier the same season above the full NTMLE hard-caps the signing team at the First Apron
Rulebook §1.5.2 is now enforced: a team already at or above the First Apron is blocked from making such a signing entirely

Fixed §4.3 contagion measuring team salary after the trade instead of before it — a team that started below the First Apron and crossed it by taking on salary escaped the hard-cap lock the rule exists to apply
New Suggestions page (/suggestions): members can file a suggestion and follow its status; BOD and admins can retriage or delete
Free Agency: never-signed free agents with no cap hold now appear alongside renounced ones, tagged Unsigned; dropped the Status column since the salary cell already carries that colour coding

New Trade Retrospectives page (/trade-retros): grades all 481 trades in league history by the Game Score each side's acquisitions actually went on to produce for the team that acquired them, filterable by season, team and grade

Trade Retrospectives credits production only from the trade's effective season onward, so a midseason trade never counts a player's production for his previous team; draft picks are listed but left unvalued unless the draft has happened and the resulting player is unambiguous

Builds now verify their own output: build/smoke_test.py checks every generated CSV still has the columns the pages read, still has rows, and has no silently-blanked column, and that every data path a page fetches exists. Runs after each build and on every commit

Rulebook §3.1: documented UFA/RFA free-agency eligibility (years of NBA experience + Qualifying Offer test) — flagged as a proposed rule pending BOD confirmation, fills the previous "pending documentation" gap
Cap Settings: added a read-only Maximum Salary (§3.11) panel per season, computed live from the Salary Cap field instead of being tracked as its own number

Transaction form: retired players (e.g. LaMarcus Aldridge) no longer appear in the player search dropdown for Trade, Guarantee Year, Void Player, Release, or Option Decision — only Free Agency Signing excluded them before

Team pages: renamed the Overview tab to Roster and added a new Team Settings tab for editing jersey numbers and a player's owner-assigned secondary position (primary position stays read-only, shown as the first position from the 2K attribute scrape)
Team Settings edits (jersey number, secondary position) are now gated strictly by the team's own role, not admin/rosters/bod
Secondary position can only be set to one of the player's own eligible positions (their bio's position list), not any of the five positions

Draft Picks table: fixed Stepien lock indicator keying by year+orig only, which could cause a 2nd round pick to be wrongly flagged STEPIEN when a locked 1st round pick shared the same year and orig team (§ 7.2 only ever applies to first-rounders)
Player pages: fixed mid-season trade rows sorting in reverse chronological order within a season (tiebreak now follows the active sort direction instead of always defaulting to most-recent-first)
Team pages: Draft Picks table column order changed to ...Swap, Frozen, Notes (Frozen now comes before Notes)

Draft Picks table: a pick that's compensation for a different pick's unresolved protection ladder now correctly shows up for the team holding that fallback claim (server-side fix), displayed under Uncertain Owner rather than a misleadingly confident Acquired

Fixed another Stepien Rule gap: a pick that's compensation for a different pick's unresolved protection ladder (ladder_fallback_of) wasn't credited toward that team's draft-year coverage at all, since neither the roster page nor /api/picks/{team}'s own filter surfaces it — could have caused a false lock on an unrelated pick in a neighboring year
CLAUDE.md: documented that same-group_id pick rows are one shared, indivisible claim (can't trade one row and keep the other) — internal documentation only, no site-facing change

Fixed a Stepien Rule bug: two pick rows sharing a swap group or binary chain were treated as independent claims, so a team could look like it had a spare when trading away either row would actually empty that draft year for them (e.g. HOU's 2027 1st, a shared DET/HOU swap right shown as two rows). Both the roster-page lock indicator and the trade validator now correctly treat same-group rows as one shared claim

CLAUDE.md: replaced the picks-conveyance doc pointer with the complete pick data model written out directly (orig/owner/leaves/group_id/protected/swap_owner/ladder/legacy) — internal documentation only, no site-facing change

CLAUDE.md: added a pointer to nbn-api/docs/picks-conveyance.md (plus a fast-recall cheat sheet on orig/owner/leaves) ahead of any pick-object interpretation — internal documentation only, no site-facing change

Team pages: reworked the Stepien Rule indicator — a whole-team "currently in violation" banner could only ever fire from a data gap (the trade that would cause it is already blocked at submit time), so it never showed anything useful. Replaced with a per-pick flag in the Draft Picks table (reusing the Frozen column) marking specifically which picks can't be traded away right now without opening a two-year gap
Team pages: added a Stepien Rule indicator on the Draft Picks section — flags when a team has no first-round pick (own or acquired) in two or more consecutive draft years (§ 7.2)
Transactions: added RFA Offer Sheet (§ 3.15) as a submittable type, with offering-team and matched/not-matched outcome fields
Team pages: added a “What If Mode” roster sandbox for previewing hypothetical roster/contract changes (attribute impact, hard-cap projection) without saving anything
Rulebook: § 3.12 and § 3.15 now show a system-enforced badge alongside manual review, documenting what the API actually checks vs. what's still committee judgment
Player pages: added a Badge History table showing 2K badges earned per snapshot
poopoo audit: added Dead Cap Status mismatch detection (sheet books a flat dead-cap charge, site still shows an active roster entry)
build/poopoo.py: anchor the Roster Cap Figures block off the “Guaranteed Salary” row label instead of a hardcoded row number, fixing a silent hard_cap=None on row-shifted team tabs
build/scrape_2k_attributes.py: added --replace-last-ovr to correct a bad prior OVR scrape entry in place instead of appending a new one

Rulebook: added § 2.1a Empty Roster Charge with two floors — a real, persisted charge (that season's rookie/0-years minimum per open slot, counted as guaranteed salary) only below 12 standard players, but trade legality is judged against the full 14-player minimum, with any gap up to 14 assumed filled at the rookie minimum for hard-cap/apron comparison purposes even when nothing posts to the real roster; § 2.1, § 3.10's cap-hold table, and § 4.5's trade roster-size rule updated to match

Rulebook: § 3.12 now embeds the real Minimum Salary Scale by years of NBA experience (0 through 10+), sourced from the actual NBA scale and updated live from the same per-season data as the § 1.1 cap table, replacing the old external-link-only reference
Added a per-season minimum-salary-scale table (min_salary_scale) to cap-levels.json and the Cap Settings admin UI, alongside the existing cap/apron/exception fields

Trade Simulator and the real trade-submission validator now compute each team's post-trade roster count and assume any gap up to 14 players gets filled at the rookie minimum when checking hard-cap/apron legality — a trade can no longer duck a hard cap by shedding headcount, even if the resulting roster count wouldn't trigger a real charge on its own

Team pages show a live "Empty Roster Charge" roster line (and count it in guaranteed salary / MLE-eligibility totals) whenever a team's real standard roster count is below 12, recomputed on every page load with no separate transaction needed

Roster tables: 2K-attribute badges collapsed from 3 loud tiers to a quiet, muted style shown inline right after the player's name (where jersey numbers used to sit); top-10% earns a badge, top-5% gets a slightly more visible outline instead of a brighter color

Roster tables: added Contracts / Stats / Ratings mode switch — Stats shows each player's per-game averages from their latest season on record, Ratings shows every individual 2K attribute with heat-map coloring; Player/Pos/Age/OVR stay fixed across all three

Site-wide: added a theme picker to the nav bar (NBN Today dark, NBN Today Light, Lavender Rose, or Match System), replacing the single hardcoded dark palette; color tokens and shared nav/search chrome moved into new css/theme.css and css/nav-chrome.css
build/scrape_2k_attributes.py now also scrapes each player's 2K badges (name, tier, category) from their "All Badges" tab and stores them per snapshot alongside attributes

Trade Simulator: supports 3+ team trades — add as many team cards as you need; with only 2 teams nothing changes, but with 3+ each selected asset gets a destination dropdown so the office can model real multi-team deals instead of just two-team swaps
Trade Simulator: added Bi-Annual Exception and Trade Exception (TPE) options alongside the MLEs for absorbing incoming salary without a matching send-back
Trade Simulator: every roster row now shows its type (Player, Two-Way, Draft Rights, or Cap Hold) so it's clear what you're actually trading

Trade Simulator: checking a Cap Hold player reveals a sign-and-trade contract-terms form (years, salary schedule, Bird rights, funding source) and validates it against the real rulebook rules — contract length, the 5% raise cap, MLE exclusion, Base Year Compensation, and the receiving team's First Apron limit

Trade Simulator: draft picks now load from the live picks API instead of a flat CSV file that hadn't been written since May and had drifted badly out of date (still listing already-drafted picks as tradeable, missing acquired picks, and mislabeling swap/protection picks)

Trade Simulator: a pick's true origin team is now sent to the validator correctly, and contingent picks (swap/protection/ladder) that collapse to one shared claim across several distinct picks no longer show as multiple duplicate selectable rows

Draft Picks tables: a pick whose real terms predate the site's conveyance model (a historical cascade too tangled to model structurally) now shows a clear "LEGACY" flag and distinct styling instead of rendering as an ordinary confident "Own" pick with the real terms hidden only in Notes prose

Draft Picks tables: when a swap or chain collapses two or more distinct picks into one row, the Team column now shows both the original picks and the current candidate owners (e.g. "DEN/OKC → BOS | OKC") instead of only the current candidates, which could misread as one team having traded its pick away entirely
Draft Picks tables: a contingent pick's Team cell now shows a tooltip linking to the real trade(s) that created it, instead of no context at all

Draft Picks tables: the Swap column now shows a clear "TEAM (better) · TEAM (worse)" description built from the pick's real priority order, instead of a single raw team abbreviation that could misread as "this team holds swap rights" when it doesn't

Draft Picks tables: stale leftover "protected"/"conditional: ..." placeholder text is no longer shown in Notes once a pick has real modeled structure (it now duplicates or contradicts the Protection/Swap columns) — genuine free-text notes are untouched
A swap group spanning multiple picks (e.g. a 2-team best-of-1st swap) now collapses to one row per team instead of listing every pick in the group separately
Team roster tables now show a small player headshot next to each name, and the jersey number appears as a #-tag after the name instead of taking its own column
Trading Block salary columns now start on the current league year (matching team roster pages) instead of a hardcoded 25-26

Added a salary filter to the Trading Block table: set a min and/or max (in $M) on any season individually — e.g. max $0 in 27-28 to find players off the books that year. Active filters show a count on the Salary button and stack together

Hovering an OVR rating on a team roster, the Trading Block, or the player index now pops up that player's full 2K attribute breakdown (tap on mobile, or focus it with the keyboard). Potential and 2K position show in the popup header
Added an Attributes filter to the Trading Block: pick any 2K attribute and set a minimum rating. Add as many as you like — they stack, so you can ask for 3PT 85+ and Block 50+ at once
Codify trade limit in rulebook § 4.5: 15 trades per season, with draft day trades and one trade-deadline-day trade exempt, effective 2026-27 (per passed Proposal #1)
Move the team Salaries chart from Frivolities into Cap Summary as its own tab, sharing one classification function with the cap table so a dollar is bucketed the same way in both views

Fix a categorization mismatch where two-way contracts always showed as a separate "Two-way" segment in the old salary chart even in seasons where they're actually an RFA/team-option hold per the cap table
WIP checkpoint: proposal voter breakdown shown as a table with each voter's team; new proposals default to no Abstain option; misc in-progress work
Fix poopoo/ diff table getting clipped on the right on mobile by making it horizontally scrollable
